sources: Names, descriptions and grades: Exophase (Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophies). PSN progress targets: PSNProfiles (trophies 43531). Guides: written for this page from the official descriptions; where a place or step is not pinned down by a source, the guide says so.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: it unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned, whenever that happens.
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and there is no shortcut to it: it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. Treat it as a finish line, not a task. Work through the roadmap in order — story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles, crime and money — and use the checklist on this page to see what is left. The two gold trophies, finishing the final mission and reaching 100% completion, are the real gates; everything else is a count or a moment along the way. If you are stuck on one trophy, leave it and finish another strand, then come back to it fresh.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if missions can be replayed; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game, so finish the mission cleanly the first time.
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this trophy comes at the very start of the story. Play through it as the game directs: follow the on-screen objectives, listen to the characters, and do not rush past the tutorial prompts, since the opening is where the game teaches movement, driving and the partner mechanics you will use everywhere else. The trophy should unlock when the mission ends and the results screen appears. If it does not, check that the mission actually completed rather than ending in a failed state, then replay it.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if chapters can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and this trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. Chapters in this series are strings of story missions, so the practical advice is simple: keep playing the story missions in order and do not get distracted by side content until the chapter is done, since a half-finished chapter earns nothing. The exact mission list for Chapter 1 is not pinned down by the official description, so we cannot name its last mission here — the trophy will tell you when the chapter itself is over. Check the in-game chapter screen if you want to see what remains.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if chapters can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 by finishing all of its story missions in order. Like the other chapter trophies, this one is a milestone, not a skill test: the game hands it to you for reaching the end of the chapter. Keep the story moving and avoid spending long stretches on side activities mid-chapter if you want it quickly. The official description does not name the chapter's missions or its length, and that detail is not yet confirmed in-game, so this guide cannot list them. When the chapter closes, the trophy unlocks automatically.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if chapters can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 and the trophy is yours. By this point in the story you will have the full map and most of the game's systems open, so the temptation is to wander — and wandering is fine, but the chapter only ends when its missions do. Play the story missions in the order the game offers them and watch for the chapter-closing beat. The official description gives no mission names, so no specific mission is named here; that is a gap in the source, not in your play. One clean run through the chapter is all it takes.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if chapters can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter, to earn this trophy. Expect the story to raise the stakes here: later chapters usually chain harder missions together, so go in with a full stock of supplies and a saved game before the chapter's big missions. The official description does not say how many missions Chapter 4 holds or which one ends it, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Finish the chapter, and the trophy unlocks as the story moves toward its finale.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if the final mission can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game. The choices trophy (Actions Speak Louder) hints the story may branch, so keep a save before the finale.
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission to earn this gold trophy. It is the story's endpoint, so it comes after Chapters 1 to 4 and every mission that leads into the finale. Before you start it, save your game, stock up, and clear any side content you care about, because the official description does not say what the game lets you do after the credits. The description also does not name the final mission, so this guide names no mission here. Play it through to the end credits and the trophy should unlock with the results screen.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if missions can be replayed; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Breakfast Run. Named story missions like this one unlock as you play through the chapters, so the way to reach it is to keep following the story rather than hunting for it on the map. The official description says nothing about where the mission starts, what it asks you to do, or which chapter it belongs to, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game — so this guide cannot give you a walkthrough step. Play the mission when the game offers it, finish its objectives, and the trophy unlocks at the results screen.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if missions can be replayed; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the mission The Cartel Heist. The name promises a heist, and heist missions in this series usually ask for preparation — a plan, a crew choice or a vehicle — before the job itself. The official description confirms none of that: it gives no starting point, no prep list and no chapter, and none of it is yet confirmed in-game. Reach the mission through the story, follow its objectives as they appear, and expect a multi-stage job. The trophy unlocks when the heist mission completes, not when the planning starts.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if missions can be replayed; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Child's Play. It is one of the named story missions, so it arrives in the course of the chapters rather than as something you can trigger early. The official description gives no location, no objectives and no chapter for it, and none of those details is yet confirmed in-game, so there is no honest walkthrough to offer here. When the mission appears, play it through to its conclusion and the trophy will unlock. If you are unsure whether you have reached it yet, check your mission log for the name.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if missions can be replayed; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Headliners. The title suggests a high-profile job, but the official description says nothing about what the mission involves, where it starts, or which chapter it sits in, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. The safe way to approach it is the same as any named story mission: keep playing the story until it is offered, save before you start, and follow the objectives the game shows you. The trophy unlocks when the mission's results screen appears, so a failed attempt that you retry still counts.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if missions can be replayed; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown, a job at the Vice City International Airport. The name points to the airport, but the official description does not confirm the mission's starting point, its objectives or its chapter, so this guide does not invent them. Reach it through the story, and when it starts, expect airport security and a getaway to feature — that is a guess from the name alone, not a confirmed step. Finish the mission and the trophy unlocks at the results screen.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if missions can be replayed; mission replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory. The military-style name suggests a large set-piece, but the official description gives no objectives, no location and no chapter, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. Do not go looking for it on the map: named missions arrive through the story. When it is offered, save first, stock up, and play through its stages as the game presents them. The trophy unlocks when the mission completes, so a failed first attempt that you retry is no problem.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.missable_note: Not missable: completion can be chased after the story ends, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — the game's own checklist of story, side content, activities and collectibles, all finished. This is the long gold trophy and the real gate before the platinum. The official description does not list what counts toward the 100%, and that list is not yet confirmed in-game, so this guide cannot spell it out. The practical approach: finish the story, then work down this page's checklist — stranger strands, activities, collectibles, exploration — and watch the in-game completion percentage climb. Leave this trophy for last and let it be the summary of everything else.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: stunts are a repeatable count you can grind anywhere, any time.
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts. A stunt, as the game counts it, is a driving feat — a jump, a near miss, a long airtime landing, a drift — and the counter climbs as you play. The fastest honest approach is to fold stunts into everything else: jump the ramps and hills you pass while travelling, and treat long drives as practice. The official description does not define exactly which moves count as stunts, and that definition is not yet confirmed in-game, so watch the counter after different moves to learn what the game rewards. 250 sounds like a lot, but it accumulates across a full playthrough.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 250. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: activities stay open after the story, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — nine types in total, according to the PSN target. This is a sampler trophy: it rewards breadth, not mastery, so you only need one go at each activity rather than a win or a high score. Work through the activities the game offers — racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, arcade games, bowling, meditation and the rest — and tick them off as you find them. The official description does not name the nine types, and that list is not yet confirmed in-game, so use the in-game activities menu as your checklist. Do one of everything and the trophy pops.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 9 types. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: range challenges can be retried, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the game's pure skill test and one of the hardest silvers: every challenge needs a gold, not just a pass. Go to the shooting range, learn each challenge's target layout and time limit, and retry the ones you miss — the description sets no limit on attempts. Start with the weapon types you are best with, use the range's practice runs to learn the timing, and save the hardest challenges for when your aim is warm. The range's location and the challenge list are not pinned down by the official description, so check the in-game range menu.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 42 challenges. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: drone races can be retried at each location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at all 14 locations. Drone racing is about the racing line: learn each course's gates before you push for speed, and use the first lap to memorise the turns. You must win at every location, so a single win is not enough — work through the locations one by one and tick them off. The official description does not name the 14 locations or where the races start, and that is not yet confirmed in-game, so use the in-game activity map to find them. A lost race costs nothing but time: retry it until you win.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 14 locations. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: races can be retried and replayed.
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word different matters: winning the same race twenty times does not count, so you need twenty distinct race events won. Pick the vehicle class and race type you are strongest in, learn the routes, and work through the race list systematically rather than repeating your favourite. The official description does not say which races count or where they start, and that is not yet confirmed in-game, so let the in-game race menu be your list. A win is a win — you do not need to beat a record, just finish first.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 20 races. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: the challenge can be retried, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a rival angler, and the challenge is a head-to-head fishing contest rather than free fishing — so you need to find Cal and take him on, not just catch fish on your own. The official description does not say where Cal fishes, when the challenge unlocks, or how it is scored, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. Practise fishing first so you know the casting and reeling mechanics, then challenge him when you are confident. If you lose, the description gives no reason to think you cannot try again.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: arcade games can be replayed.
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Find an arcade machine, pick any game on it, and play it through to its end — completion, not a high score, is what the trophy asks for. The official description does not name the arcade games, say where the machines are, or say what counts as completing one, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. Choose the shortest or simplest game on the machine, learn its controls from its own instructions, and finish a full run. It is one of the easiest trophies on the list once you find a machine.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if stranger missions can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. Stranger missions are side strands given by characters you meet around Leonida: you take their jobs one at a time until the strand ends with a final mission. To reach Andy's, find him in the world and work through his missions in order. The official description does not say where Andy is, how many missions his strand holds, or what the final mission asks, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. Keep an eye out for his marker on the map, finish each job he offers, and the trophy unlocks at the strand's end.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if stranger missions can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's strand. Like the other stranger strands, Kenton's is a chain of side missions that ends with a finale — the trophy is for that last mission, not for starting the strand. Find Kenton, take his jobs as they appear, and play them in order. The official description gives no location for Kenton, no mission count and no details of the finale, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. The boat in the title hints at where the finale may take place, but that is a guess from the name, not a confirmed step.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if stranger missions can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's strand. Billy's missions are side content, so they unlock as you explore and meet him — not through the main story. Work through his jobs in the order he offers them until the strand's final mission appears. The official description does not say where Billy is found, how many missions his strand has, or what the finale involves, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. The lone rider name suggests a solo ride, but that is a guess from the title alone. Finish the finale and the trophy is yours.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: strands stay open after the story, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Complete eight mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Each strand is a chain of side missions for one character — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have one, and there are more to find. The count is eight, so you need more than the five named strands: explore the map, watch for stranger markers, and take every side job you find. The official description does not name all eight strangers or their locations, and that list is not yet confirmed in-game. Finish a strand fully — a half-finished strand does not count — and keep count on this page.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 8 strands. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if stranger missions can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's strand. Randy's jobs, judging by the title, revolve around supply — but the official description confirms nothing about his missions, his location or the finale, and none of it is yet confirmed in-game. Find Randy in the world, accept his missions as they come, and play the strand to its end. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so do not leave a strand half-finished if you can help it. The trophy unlocks when Randy's last mission completes.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description if stranger missions can be replayed; replay has not yet been confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's strand. Tyrone is another of the strangers with a mission chain that ends in a finale, and the trophy is for that final mission. The official description gives no location, no mission count and no details of the finale, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game, so this guide cannot walk you to him. Meet him in the world, work through his jobs in order, and finish the last one. Together with the other four named strangers, Tyrone's strand is one of the eight that the Strangers & Freaks silver counts.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: meditation spots stay available after the story, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. These are quiet scenic spots scattered around the map, and the trophy is a collectible hunt in disguise: visit each one and meditate there. Work through them systematically — by region, so you do not miss one — and check the in-game map for markers, since the official description does not list the spots and their locations are not yet confirmed in-game. There is no time limit and no skill test: the challenge is finding all eighteen. Pair this with the exploration trophy and the WAiNK spots to save travel time.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 18 spots. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: the hunt can be retried, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret wants one particular animal — a unique one, not just any wildlife — so this is a tracking job, not a random hunt. Find Bret, take the job, and follow the hunt as the game presents it: track the animal, get into range, and take the shot cleanly. The official description does not say which animal it is, where it lives, or where Bret is found, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. Go in with a suitable weapon and patience, and if the animal escapes, the description gives no reason to think the hunt cannot be tried again.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: cards stay findable after the story, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Complete three collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida, and a set is complete only when you hold every card in it — so this trophy is a scavenger hunt with a checklist. Pick one set at a time, search its locations, and keep track of which cards you still need. The official description does not say how many cards are in a set, how many sets exist, or where the cards are, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. Pair the search with your exploration of the 52 areas: you will pass card locations on the way. Three full sets is the goal.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 3 sets. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: WAiNK spots stay available after the story, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is an in-game activity you perform at marked spots — the description treats it as something you do at a place, and the count is one hundred, so this is a long grind best done gradually. As you travel for other trophies, stop at every WAiNK spot you pass and use it; the count will climb without dedicated farming. The official description does not explain what WAiNK It is or where the spots are, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Do not leave all one hundred for the end: spread them across the playthrough.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 100 locations. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: challenges are repeatable objectives you can keep working on.
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's side objectives — small tasks the game tracks across your play, from driving feats to combat and exploration. Fifty is a large number, but they accumulate naturally: play the story, try the activities, and check the challenges menu regularly to see which ones are close to done. The official description does not list the challenges or say which count, and that list is not yet confirmed in-game. The practical approach is to let this trophy fill itself while you chase the others, then mop up the nearest ones at the end.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 50. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missable_note: Timing-sensitive: the wanted level must be lost with your partner present, in one escape. If your partner is not with you, or you are caught, the attempt fails — set it up deliberately with your partner beside you and a fast vehicle ready.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner and escape. The key condition is togetherness: your partner must be with you when the heat is lost, so start the attempt with them in the car. Raise your wanted level to four stars, then break line of sight and stay out of the search area until the stars clear — use a fast vehicle, quiet roads and the map's edge rather than fighting the police. The official description does not say how the partner is summoned or where to hide, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Save before you try, and do not attempt it while carrying other risks.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 4 stars. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missable_note: Timing-sensitive: three robberies in a row with your partner, keeping the wanted level the whole time. If the wanted level drops — or you are caught — the chain breaks and you start over. Pick three shops close together and plan the route first.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. This is a chain, and the chain is the hard part: the wanted level must stay up across all three robberies, so you cannot stop to hide or wait between them. Plan a route through three nearby shops, keep your partner with you, and move fast from one to the next. The official description does not name which shops count or how close together they must be, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. If the chain breaks, you start over — nothing is lost but time.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 3 shops. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: vehicles keep appearing across the map, and discovery is a cumulative count.
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery means finding a vehicle type you have not seen before, so the count climbs as you explore new areas and meet new traffic — a hundred distinct vehicles is a lot, but it accumulates across the whole game. Drive everywhere, visit car parks, dealerships and quiet neighbourhoods, and take a moment to look at what is parked around you. The official description does not list the vehicles or say exactly what counts as discovering one, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Pair this with exploration of the 52 areas: new areas bring new vehicles.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 100 vehicles. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.missable_note: Timing-sensitive: all five takedowns must happen inside one use of Combat Focus. If the focus ends with only four down, the attempt fails — set it up where enemies cluster and save first.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is a slow-time aiming mode, and the trophy needs five takedowns before it runs out — so you need a spot where at least five enemies are close together, and you need to be quick and accurate. Find a busy fight, trigger Combat Focus when the enemies are grouped, and work through them without wasting time. The official description does not say how Combat Focus is activated or how long it lasts, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. If you fall short, reload and try again in a busier spot.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 5 enemies. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missable_note: Timing-sensitive: the departure must be unscheduled, which suggests a specific trick at the airport rather than a normal exit. Save before you try it at VCIA, and expect to experiment.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the Vice City International Airport. An unscheduled departure means leaving the airport in a way the game does not expect — the obvious reading is stealing a plane and taking off, but the official description does not say that, and it is not yet confirmed in-game. Go to the airport, look for a plane you can reach, and try to get airborne without following the normal route out. Save before you try, since airport security is likely to respond, and expect the attempt to need more than one go.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: it is a combat moment with tanks that can be retried, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: The description is a joke — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — and the Rhinos are tanks, so this trophy involves dealing with a Rhino tank. The official description does not say whether you must steal one, destroy one, survive one or drive one, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game, so this guide will not pretend to know. The honest approach: when you meet a Rhino in the game, engage with it — try to take it on, and if that does not trigger the trophy, try the other obvious interaction. Keep a save before the encounter so you can retry it.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.missable_note: Timing-sensitive: the robbery must be completed without being detected. Being spotted fails the attempt — plan the approach, save first, and restart if you are seen.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the whole trophy: you need to get in, take the goods and get out without any alarm or witness. Scout the store first, learn where the staff and cameras are, move quietly, and take the quietest route in and out. The official description does not name the store or say what counts as being detected, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Save before the attempt so a failed run costs nothing, and if you are spotted, reload and try a different approach rather than fighting your way out.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: vaults are a repeatable count of five, each ending in an escape.
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape from each one. A vault robbery is a two-part job: break into the vault, then get away clean — the escape counts, so do not relax once the money is in hand. Plan each getaway before you go in, with a fast vehicle and a route away from the police. The official description does not say where the vaults are, how they are opened, or whether all five are available from the start, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. Five vaults, five escapes, and the silver is yours.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 5 vaults. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: armored trucks are a repeatable robbery you can attempt again.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida, so the first step is finding one on the move — watch the traffic in busy districts and look for the distinctive truck. Stop it, deal with its guards, take what is inside, and then escape before the police close in. The official description does not say where trucks run or how to open one, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Save before the attempt, plan your escape route first, and treat the getaway as half the job.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: areas stay visitable after the story, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — all 52 areas of the state. This is the map-completion trophy: every named area must be visited, from Vice City itself to the swamps, beaches and small towns. Work through the map region by region and watch the area name appear on screen as you enter somewhere new; the in-game map and its area counter are your checklist, since the official description does not list the 52 areas and that list is not yet confirmed in-game. Fold this into every other trophy: travel to a new activity and you will tick off areas on the way.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 52 areas. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: illegal operations are a repeatable count across the nine gangs.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the nine gangs. Every gang in Leonida runs illegal operations, and this trophy wants one hit against each of them — nine robberies, nine different gangs. Learn which gangs operate where, pick one operation per gang, and keep a note of which gangs you have already hit so you do not waste time repeating one. The official description does not name the nine gangs or their operations, and that list is not yet confirmed in-game. Work through them as you explore: new areas mean new gangs.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 9 gangs. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: a cocktail on Ocean Beach can be had any time you visit.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a scene trophy: go to Ocean Beach, find somewhere to order a cocktail, and take in the view. The official description does not say which bar or spot counts, and that is not yet confirmed in-game — so head for the beachfront, look for a bar with a view, and order a drink there. It is one of the gentlest trophies on the list and a good one to pick up early, while you are still learning the map. If the first bar does not trigger it, try another spot along the beach.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: a showroom smash can be retried, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The classic style is the giveaway: drive a car straight through the showroom window and out the other side, the way the series has always done it. Find a vehicle showroom, get a car inside or aimed at it, and drive through the glass. The official description does not name the showroom or say exactly what counts as smashing out, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Save first, pick a fast car, and aim for the widest window. One clean smash should do it.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: bowling can be played again any time.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. Go to the alley, start a game of bowling and play it through — the follow-through in the description suggests completing a game, or at least a full frame, rather than just walking in. The official description does not say how many frames count or where the alley is beyond its name, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Play a full game to be safe, and enjoy it: bowling is one of the game's quiet activities, and the trophy is for playing it properly, not for a particular score.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: a partnership moment that the story will present, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and the official list gives nothing more: no mission name, no activity, no location, and none of it is yet confirmed in-game. The honest reading is that this is a partner moment in the story, something that happens when you and your partner do something the public notices. Play the story with your partner, take on the partner activities as they appear, and watch for a moment that fits the description. This guide cannot name the trigger, because no source does.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description, but choices may branch the story: PSN tracks a count to 500, so keep choosing — and keep a save before big decisions until branching is confirmed in-game.
trophies.guide: Make choices — for better or worse. PSN tracks a count for this trophy, up to 500, which suggests it is about the sheer number of choices you make across the game rather than one single decision. The official description does not say which choices count, where they appear, or what the count measures, and none of that is yet confirmed in-game. The practical advice is to play naturally and make decisions whenever the game offers them, rather than always taking the same path. Watch the counter in the PSN trophy list to learn what it is counting.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 500 choices. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: succeeding on a second try is something that happens naturally when you retry things.
trophies.guide: The description is a riddle — 'second time's the charm' — and the official list gives nothing more, so the honest reading is that this trophy pops when you succeed at something on your second attempt after failing the first. That could be a mission, a challenge or an activity. Do not force it: play normally, retry what you fail, and it is likely to unlock on its own. The official description does not say which attempt counts or what must be retried, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. If it has not popped late in the game, try failing and then passing a short activity.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missable_note: Timing-sensitive: it asks you to witness something strange, which sounds like a one-off event in the world. Explore odd places and keep a save when something unusual starts — it may not repeat.
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. The description — 'What the hell just happened?' — points to a random or hidden event in the world, the kind of odd sighting this series hides in odd corners of the map. Explore unusual places, visit at odd hours, and pay attention when something out of the ordinary happens. The official description does not say what the event is or where it happens, and that is not yet confirmed in-game, so this guide cannot point you to it. Keep exploring, and when something strange does happen, the trophy should follow.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.missable_note: Timing-sensitive: a melee drive-by means striking someone with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle. Set it up deliberately — a slow vehicle, a clear target — and save first.
trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by — hit a person with a melee weapon while driving past them. The trick is the combination: you need a moving vehicle, a melee weapon in hand, and a target close enough to the road to reach. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, swing as you pass, and keep going. The official description does not say how many people count or which weapon to use, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Practise the timing on a quiet road, and expect a few misses before it lands.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: laundering is a cumulative total you can keep working on.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills are dirty money from robberies, and laundering turns them into clean cash — the trophy counts the total laundered, not a single job. Rob, collect the bills, and hand them to your contacts to wash, repeating until the counter reaches $250,000. The official description does not name the contacts or say where laundering happens, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Pair this with the vault and truck robberies: the money from those jobs is the raw material for this total.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of $250,000. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: spending is a cumulative total across all shops.
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. The counter is cumulative and counts every shop in the game, so the money you spend naturally — on weapons, clothes, food and vehicles — all adds up. There is no need to waste money: just play, buy what you need, and check the total as you go. If you reach the endgame short of the mark, top it up with useful purchases rather than throwing cash away. The official description does not say which shops count, and that list is not yet confirmed in-game, but every shop you use should contribute.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of $100,000. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: garages stay for sale after the story, as far as the official description shows.
trophies.guide: Purchase all eight garage properties. Garages are property you buy to store vehicles, and the trophy needs every one of them owned. Save your money for them, buy them as you find them for sale, and keep a note of which ones you already own. The official description does not say where the eight garages are or what they cost, and that is not yet confirmed in-game, so use the in-game property listings to find them. Eight garages is a significant spend, so pair this with the money-making trophies and buy the cheaper ones first.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 8 garages. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.missable_note: Not missable from its description: vehicles can be registered any time through the app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is an in-game phone app for vehicles: find a vehicle, open the app, and register it — then repeat with nine more. Different vehicles count, so use the variety you meet while discovering the hundred vehicles for Whip It Good. The official description does not say which vehicles count or how the app works, and that is not yet confirmed in-game. Keep a mix of cars, bikes and anything else you find, register each new one as you go, and the trophy pops at ten.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — name, description and grade; PSNProfiles — PSN progress target of 10 vehicles. Guide: our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
